rationale: Both use the same coefficient-sum backtracking with letters sorted by weight. A's pruning is a precomputed suffix bound array checked with one comparison, abs(sum) > bound[i], which is easy to verify and cheap. B's boundsOK recomputes available digits and min/max ranges at every node. That is well documented and a bit tighter, but it adds a fair amount of machinery the problem does not need. B has small robustness extras: an early exit for more than ten letters and space stripping. Its addWord place-value loop is also cleaner than A's awkward inner loop for computing powers. On balance A is simpler and clearer overall with no loss of correctness, so it edges ahead.
